terms.meaning: Code that runs in the user's browser rather than on the server.
Values the page remembers while it runs, such as the selected document.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and browser setting
sections.what: Loads the page building blocks, translations, evidence grouping, and types. Marks the file to run in the browser.
sections.why: Needed because the page responds to clicks and uses state.
sections.watch_out: Because it runs in the browser, it cannot read server-only data directly.

sections.name: DocumentWorkflow
sections.title: Document card with inspect button
sections.what: Shows one document card with an Inspect button that marks it as selected.
sections.why: Lets the user open a document's details one at a time.
sections.watch_out: The button refers to an element with the id extracted-fields that appears only when a document is selected.

sections.name: DocumentsContent
sections.title: Main documents content
sections.what: Holds the page logic: loading samples, selecting a document, running extraction, and showing core and supporting evidence with the sample panel.
sections.why: Keeps the page's behavior in one place.
sections.watch_out: Failed extraction and a failed sample list both fall back quietly, so a problem may look like an empty page.

sections.name: DocumentsPage
sections.title: Page entry point
sections.what: Wraps the content in the case loader so it receives the case details.
sections.why: Lets the page load the right case before showing content.

summary: The documents page for a case. It shows core and supporting evidence, runs extraction on demand, and adds sample documents.
purpose: Gives the user one place to review documents and their extracted fields.
why: Likely reason: core and supporting evidence are separated, and a safety note is shown, to make clear which items matter most.
how: The page wraps its content in the case layout. The content loads the sample list, groups evidence, and tracks the selected document. Inspect shows the source text. Run extraction sends a request to the extract address and shows the fields or a failure message. Sample buttons attach a fixture through the case actions.
inputs: Case detail, case id, the chosen language, and the sample list from the server.
outputs: The rendered page, extraction results, and error text.
risks: Extraction failures show a generic message. A failed sample list is quietly replaced with an empty list. Some lines are cut off in the source.
debug: If extraction fails, check the response from the extract address. If samples are missing, check listFixtures in the case actions.
